description: DID-document fetch failure classification (RFC-ACDP-0001 §5.11 step 3; scenarios D–E also §5.11 'Caching' (0.5.0)). A non-2xx response, timeout or TLS failure is transient (key_resolution_unreachable); a parse failure or a fragment absent after a fresh fetch is permanent (key_resolution_failed). Pins an existing rule: an implementation that maps a DID-host outage to a permanent verdict feeds a false 'permanently invalid' into revocation discovery (RFC-ACDP-0014 §8). Applies to registries (producer DIDs at publish) and consumers alike. SSRF refusals stay permanent and are pinned by did-ssrf-*.

scenarios.name: C — 200 with a body that is not JSON
D — no verificationMethod matches the fragment after one forced re-fetch

expected.behavior: (0.5.0) The verdict from the fresh document is final.

scenarios.name: E — fragment absent from the stale cache, forced re-fetch declined by the rate limit

expected.behavior: (0.5.0) A step-4 absence from a stale document is never reported as permanent.

notes: Behavioral; not executed by scripts/conformance-runner.py. Scenarios A–C are conditional on nothing (RFC-ACDP-0001 §5.11 step 3 is Final); D–E bind 0.5.0 verifiers.
